fics.title: and we all fall down
fics.summary:
Summary:

The truth was, yeah, Shane married Ilya, but he’d married hockey first. He married hockey the second he signed his rookie contract with the Metros, and his courtship began long, long before. And his marriage to hockey wasn’t like his marriage to Ilya. Hockey wouldn’t ever love him back. Ilya wasn’t going to chew Shane up and spit him out at some nebulous point after he turned thirty and before he turned forty, his joints busted and his mouth full of dentures and his brain fucked to hell and back. And that marriage—his first marriage—had always come before his second, illicit shotgun wedding.

It wasn’t ideal, maybe, but that was just how things were. Hell, it was probably the same for Ilya, too. The fuck was Shane supposed to do about it? Nothing, nothing, nothing. He liked his life just the way it was. He didn’t want to do anything different. He still doesn’t. And that’s the worst, most shameful part of it all: at the end of the day, some part of Shane will always wish he could wind back time like adjusting a watch; erase that Instagram post before it ever hit the internet and go back to the life they’d had before; the life that was slowly killing them both.

Summary:

Shane doesn’t like social media. For one, he’s so used to shoving his private life so deep in the closet that it can’t see the light of day, but also, he’s a naturally private person, and the thought of letting people see any part of what keeps him stable and going–it scares him. So mostly, his social media accounts are run by his mom and his social media team, mostly ads and sponsorships and sharing Metros posts and information from the Irina Foundation.

Every once in a blue moon, it’s something truly him, the cottage or him and Hayden and JJ, a yoga mat (a tuna melt, a coke, a loon at the cottage).

And then, just like that (and one ill-timed Fanmail video), his carefully curated private world implodes, and while picking up the pieces, he decides he’s done.

He has this amazing life, this amazing boyfriend (fiancé!), and he wants the world to know at least a piece of it because he and Ilya deserve to finally be openly in love.

Summary:

They’re only standing like that for about a minute, if even, when Hollander decides to make conversation, “So, uh, are your parents here with you?”

Ilya just nods. His mom is here with him, of course she is. She wouldn’t want to be anywhere else and Ilya doesn’t think he appreciates her enough for that, but he tries. As best as he can, at least.

“That’s nice, mine are too,” Hollander says quietly with a smile and they fall back into that earlier silence, listening just to those same sounds.

Skates on ice.

Sticks hitting pucks.

Each other’s breathing.

After a few minutes, Hollander awkwardly clears his throat and takes a step back, “Anyway, uh, I should probably go. My parents, they’re waiting on me, but um…” He trails off and Ilya notices the hesitation in his voice before he takes his hand out of his pocket and holds it out to Ilya again, smiling, “good luck in the tournament.”

Summary:

As she watched Rozanov skate half circles around Shane's unconscious body in the unnatural quiet of the Boston arena, Jackie Pike's heart raced. Her whole body shook as her brain struggled to make sense of what was happening. A few moments later, she recognized the Russian's expression. She'd seen it on the faces of other WAGs when their men went down hard. It was the physical manifestation of her recurring nightmare - Hayden motionless and bleeding after a hit, thinking she was about to lose the love of her life. Nothing else existed but that body lying on the ice.

This was exactly how Rozanov looked at him now, and the only possible explanation was love.

Or,

Ilya knows that, between him and Shane, he's the more affectionate of the two. Summary:

Svetlana could give Ilya everything Shane could not.

She shared his language, his culture, and knew what it was like living in Russia–she didn’t have to try and learn Russian in secret so if Ilya wanted to just talk freely with her he could. She’d known Ilya his whole life, known his father and brother and, most importantly, his mother–the most precious person to Ilya. She could date Ilya, in public, and it wouldn’t cause a scandal–Ilya wouldn’t have to sacrifice his country to be with her or have to secure citizenship somewhere safe just so that if people found out he wouldn’t get arrested. She could stay with Ilya during the hockey season and share his space–she could get groceries with him and argue with him in the produce aisle about what to make for dinner that week. She could love Ilya, freely, and Shane could not.

In the end it was not about Ilya or even Svetlana at all really. It was about what Shane could not be, what he could not give, to the person he loved most.

"Shane slipped out into the freezing air. He took a deep breath, his eyes scanning for familiar Russian curls shimmering under the streetlights.

Summary:

Shane and Ilya's first hockey camp is going swimmingly, and playing house at his parents' in Ottawa ain't so bad, either.

Watching Ilya with a line of kids lapping the rink to warm up had given me what I guess straight people refer to as ‘baby fever’. They bring out the kid in him, and not one who’s terrified and deeply sad but one who always wants to play, the side of him that will take wrestling around in bed a little too seriously and always wants to turn everything into a joke or game. He’d led the line of kids, calling after them, “come on my little ducklings!”, each of them keeping a puck handled tightly in front of them, picking up speed and getting a little more challenging each lap. When they’d moved on to slapshots, Ilya stopped the first one to make it into the net before she could go back to the end of the line, telling her very seriously, “Okay, now is most important part: now you say, давай!” He threw up his arms and shouted it, let’s go! The player repeated it and shyly thrust her stick up in the air. He did this with each scoring shot and then at the end with everyone to celebrate that they had finished the drills.

Summary:

Finally committed to each other, Shane and Ilya ring in a new year with some brave choices.

 

Even from here in the city, the sky is brilliantly clear and leaning back against the brick and looking up, I can see stars glittering. I pull out a cigarette and light it, taking a long first drag and letting it out with a sigh. “Goodbye, old friend,” I tell it in Russian, holding it up between thumb and forefinger. “You’ve been a great comfort, but it’s time to part ways.” I smoke in silence after that, hearing a few smaller fireworks already going off somewhere a few streets over, the whistle of a bottle rocket and the double pop. The passing of years is, to a point, quite arbitrary, but there is something about these cold, long, dark nights when the air is polished clear and clean and the stars shimmer a little brighter that draws me into reflection every year. Sometimes it’s good, reminding me of all the highlights and successes. Sometimes it reminds me how little I’ve done, how much my life is a blur of hockey and hockey-adjacent activities, but not a whole lot else.

Except of course for Shane. There is always Shane.

“You know what that sounds like, baby?” Yuna said carefully. “You could lose—”

“I don’t care!” Shane snapped. “Let everyone think I’m a slut, a whore—I don’t care! I don’t fucking care about my reputation—or, or endorsement money! Don’t tell me I need to represent—”

“No, baby,” Yuna interrupted softly. “I meant hockey. You could lose hockey.”

Hockey.

Shane froze.

Hockey had run in his blood since he put on his first pair of skates at four. Hockey shaped his brain. Hockey was why he ate, why he moved, why he dreamed. Hockey was how he made a living, how he found joy when he was free. Hockey connected him to everyone he loved. Hockey was what he was good for. Hockey was his name.

Hockey was the purpose of Shane Hollander’s existence.

Tears ran silently down his face.

Inside, he felt strangely hollow.

“I… want him back,” he managed to choke out. “I need Ilya back here with me. I NEED him safe.”

fics.summary:
Summary:

The first thing you should know about time loops is that they’re really fucking hard to break. The second thing is that you can never break one in such a way that it is incapable of returning.

The third thing you should know is that everyone around you has probably been stuck in a time loop at one point or another, and they made it out alive. This is only comforting if you’re a numbers guy, or if you’re the kind of guy who talks to others about how it feels to live the same day over and over and over and over and over and over again.

Shame if you’re not; the most important thing you should know about breaking a time loop is that it helps to tell someone you’re trapped in one in the first place.

Finding your soulmate is supposed to be beautiful. You stand in front of someone and you say their full name; they say yours. Your soulmarks appear somewhere on your bodies, and it's supposed to be beautiful. Life-changing.

It's not supposed to happen a week before the World Juniors tournament in a dirty Saskatchewan parking lot. It's not supposed to be Canada's newest darling hockey player and your future rival who whispers your name. It's not supposed to be a boy that your skin blooms for.

And if that happens, somehow, you're definitely not supposed to kiss him less than a year later. And then later. And then later. fics.title: After the Fight
fics.summary:
Summary:

After The Quiet Fight, the battle was supposed to be over.

Ilya survived cancer. He made it back to the NHL. He finished his first season back on the ice. From the outside, it looks like a victory.

But survival doesn’t mean peace.

This sequel picks up in the aftermath—when the adrenaline fades and the real cost begins to surface. Ilya is fighting a body that still hasn’t fully forgiven him. Shane is fighting a mind shaped by months of fear, hospitals, and the constant threat of loss. And together, they’re fighting each other—trying to love, plan a future, and breathe again while remission looms quietly in the background.

This is a story about what comes after the battle, when Shane and Ilya are learning how to live when they are no longer in crisis—but not free from it either. A story about the tension between gratitude and grief, strength and fragility, love and resentment.

The fight feels louder than ever.

fics.summary:
Summary:

After coming to terms with the way they feel about each other, Ilya and Shane settle into something more than they'd been before in the sanctuary of Shane's lakeside cottage.

 

Somewhere in the mist, loons chirp and call to each other, a skittering sound cut through with the long, mournful tones. The sun is up but the sky is grey, turning everything a kind of monochrome in the watery light. The placid mornings are heavenly enough that you’ve chosen the lake’s flat waters to watch this morning over coffee instead of laying in bed watching Shane sleep. It had been a hard decision, but there’s a lot on your mind, and some nagging voice in your head says they’re thoughts you can’t think in Shane’s presence lest your forehead turn to glass and he sees every thought and fancy. You know he can’t, but you know also he’s learning to read you, that your guards are down enough with him that you forget to cover everything in sarcasm and subterfuge. He’d know. If he saw you now with your mouth twisted in a contemplative little squiggle and your coffee going cold in its mug, he’d know that you’re thinking serious thoughts about him.

Ilya never texted Shane back. He didn’t call. Twenty minutes turned into two hours, then eight.
Shane had spent that time spiraling. It’s something he hasn’t done recently, at least, not about this. No, up until yesterday he thought his relationship was unflappable, that Ilya was just as happy as he was. Well, as happy as they both could be keeping such a major part of their lives a secret.

Every time he closed his eyes he saw the hurt that flashed across Ilya’s face right before he kicked him out.

I already chose you, Hollander.

The words had landed in his gut like a rock. They never discussed the things he’d given up, not because Shane wasn’t, at least peripherally, aware that that was the case. He moved to a new country and signed with a team that was so historically bad they were a laughing stock. One of the greatest players in the league tore up his American visa, sold his car collection, and moved to Ottawa just to be within driving distance of him. fics.summary:
Summary:

Shane wasn't looking back at him. He assumed that Ilya would be paying attention to the game, not its spectators. Sofia was sat upright in his lap. He was moving her back and forth to follow the puck. Ilya could see his mouth moving, even at this distance- no doubt he was explaining the rules to her infant ears. Hockey would be her first language.

Sofia was more interested in the person holding her than the game. She tipped her little head back, back, back until she was looking up at her dad. The two of them smiled, and then Shane leaned down ever so slightly.

He was brushing their noses together in the softest little nuzzle Ilya had ever seen. When he was done, Shane pressed a kiss onto her forehead.

At twenty-three, Shane Hollander was convinced that life after hockey would be empty. He couldn't imagine a world where he'd be completely happy without the focus and drive that came with playing a professional sport.

By thirty-seven, Shane was convinced that life after hockey was better. Who needed skates and sticks when your daughter was looking up at you with such a perfect, tiny smile, and your husband was winning games for all three of you?

Only one player in the league is as good at keeping a secret as Ilya Rozanov. That player is Scott Hunter. In an alternate book/show hybrid timeline, Shane Hollander spirals after his fight with Hunter in Montreal when a video of the altercation quickly makes the rounds on twitter and gets the fans talking. When Shane and Ilya confront Scott Hunter together, Hunter learns more than he ever expected. In the aftermath, Scott realizes his decision to stay in the closet has consequences he never considered - and implications for more players than just himself. And Shane and Ilya have the experience of the two halves of their lives crashing together that makes their own closet start to feel a little too small.

A bittersweet blend of emotional slow burn and spice in this canon-adjacent work explores the implications of Scott Hunter clocking it and narrates the stretch of time that ties the Montreal fight to the Tuna Meltdown in 2014.

Shane Hollander is a hockey legend known as "The Golden Alpha of Canada:" and Captain of the Montreal Voyagers.  To the roaring crowds, he’s cocky, dominant, untouchable Alpha they want in a hockey star. Yet, behind every goal, Shane hides a secret that could destroy everything he's built up. He isn’t an Alpha at all. Born Omega in a world where Omegas are sidelined from traditional "Alpha" sports, Shane’s entire career is built on a lie: daily suppressants, fake scent, relentless self-control. The cost is soul-deep exhaustion and the constant fear that a single mistake will cost him not just his trophies, but his identity.

Enter Ilya Rozanov, known as “The Dirty Russian” by fans and foes alike, a brutal, magnetic Alpha who’s battled his own demons to make it on the Voyager team. Growing up in the shadow of an abusive father who threw him into sports to "make me fucking rich", Ilya learned to survive by being harder, meaner, and utterly unbreakable. Hockey is his way out, but family obligations and old scars still chain him down..

When a chance encounter lets Ilya see Shane for who he truly is, both men are forced to confront the walls they’ve built, around their histories, their bodies, and their hearts.

Shane Hollander is done hiding. After a decade of suffocating under the colors of the Montreal Metros, a locker room defined by toxic silence and the bigotry of teammates like JJ, Shane finally makes the jump everyone said would break the league. Between homophobic chirps at the face-off dot and a front office hoping for a scandal, Shane and Ilya have a different plan. They aren't just looking for a win; they’re looking for a statement.

fics.summary:
Ilya Rozanov's life takes an unexpected turn when a deadly plane crash in 2021 takes his life, right after a fight with his long-time partner, Shane Hollander.  Though instead of the afterlife, Ilya is sent back to December 2008, just before his NHL career began, on the very day that he first met Shane. He finds himself in a familiar world, with knowledge of both the future and knowledge of the man he loves and the friends he holds dear.

As Ilya navigates this new reality, he rebuilds his relationship with Shane, who is still finding his path in both hockey and his identity as a gay man. With their rivalry blossoming into a different experience than the one Ilya experienced the first time around, the two face challenges around acceptance, family pressures, and the struggles of being openly gay and lovers in the sports world. Throughout their journey, Ilya contemplates his first life, cherishes the present, and strives to alter the course of their futures (and the futures of their friends) for the better.

Or, Ilya Rozanov discovers first hand what the butterfly effect is, and how it can drastically alter the future.

fics.summary:
”Rozanov looks good in Russia, sure, but here? I don’t know if he’ll hold up.”

Shane wasn’t supposed to be listening. At sixteen, a decade into competition hockey, this was his first time at the Saskatchewan arena and he’d taken the wrong turn in the long, echoing corridors. The conference room door was shut, but there was a crack at the bottom and the words spilled out into the hallway, bouncing off the cheap vinyl tiles. He tried to breathe quietly, desperate for news about his opponent. There was only one other player near Shane’s level, and he’d come all the way from Russia.

“The rumors—”

The voice trailed off. Someone cleared their throat.

Heart beating double-time, Shane felt for his scent blockers. One firm cuff around each wrist, pads on either side of his neck. The underwear everyone wore, basic manners. Too many alphas in a small enough space could—had—led to fights in the locker room. Always, Shane had to set a good example. Had to be better, so he could play.

“I don’t believe it.” A chair creaked. “No fuckin’ omega plays like Rozanov.”

fics.title: Love me again
fics.summary:
Shane Hollander and Ilya Rozanov are solid.

Married. Stable. Established. The NHL’s favorite “we didn’t see that coming” love story turned domestic success.

They have a house. A dog that likes Ilya better. A shared calendar that Shane actually uses.

They’ve learned how to grocery shop without arguing about brands of pasta.

They are, objectively, fine.

Which is precisely the problem.

Somewhere between sponsorship shoots, playoff runs, and arguing over whose turn it is to unload the dishwasher, the fire that once burned hot enough to survive secrecy and rivalry has… softened. Not gone. Not broken. Just familiar.
Comfortable. Predictable.

When a league marketing campaign crowns them “Hockey’s Ultimate Love Story” and assigns a documentary crew to follow them around for the season, Shane jokingly tells Ilya:
“Guess you’re going to have to fall in love with me again on camera.”

Ilya smirks. “Please. I could make you fall in love with me again in one week.”

It’s a joke.

Until it becomes a challenge.

Once outside, he leaned forward and put his hand against the cold stone wall. His phone was still to his ear, the message still recording. 
“Ilya. Please. Please. I can’t do this. I don’t know what to do. Please. You can’t be dead.” His voice broke on the word. “I love you. I love you so much. More than anything. I need to hear your voice. I need you to…I need you…I need you…fuck. Please Ilya, please.” 
Shane took the phone away from his ear and held it between both hands as though he were praying. He realized he was on the floor and didn’t know how he got there. He was crying. He was fairly certain he was hyperventilating. 
His brain was desperately trying to grab at anything. Any thread of logic. Any idea of what to do next. 
I have to see him. 
Yes. That made sense. Shane needed to get to Tampa. Now. He would go there. He would find Ilya. Ilya would be fine. They would be together. He would see him. Tell him how much he loved him. He had to go. He had to go now.
